seo.meta_title: Why You Shouldn't Say '당신' for 'You' in Korean | AI Translation Mistake
seo.meta_description: AI translators turn every 'you' into '당신', which can sound cold or even confrontational in Korean. Learn how Koreans actually address each other.

ai_failure.situation: Asking a coworker or acquaintance a simple question, like 'Did you eat lunch?'
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Outputs '당신은 점심을 먹었습니까?', mapping English 'you' directly to 당신.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: In conversation, 당신 addressed to a peer or stranger can sound distant or even like the start of an argument. Korean usually drops 'you' or uses a name/title instead.

natural_solution.rule: Drop 'you' when context is clear, or use the person's name + title. Reserve 당신 for spouses, song lyrics, ads, or written text.

alternatives.context: No pronoun at all — the most natural default
Name + 씨 for colleagues of similar rank

nuance: Korean doesn't have a neutral, all-purpose 'you'. Speakers position each other through names, titles and kinship terms (선배님, 언니, 사장님), or simply omit the subject. 당신 survives in a few special registers: between married couples, in poetry and song, in advertising copy, and — spoken with an edge — in quarrels ('당신이 뭔데?'). Because AI defaults to 당신, learners often sound either like a textbook or like they're picking a fight.
